findings.evidence: conflicting-candidate-integration-repair/design.md: "No mergeability. The conflict signal stays merge-tree in _prepare. GitHub mergeable is not read." The change adds only a merge-tree conflict check inside the RederivationEnvironmentFailed handler (publication_queue.py ~1904). A conflict that is neither a generated-only conflict nor a RederivationEnvironmentFailed conflict relies on pre-existing routing that this diff does not touch.
findings.summary: Requirement item 3 is phrased in terms of GitHub mergeable=CONFLICTING. T1 keeps `merge-tree` in `_prepare` as the only conflict signal and does not read GitHub mergeability. It is compatible with the outcome only if a waiting candidate with no red gate always reaches `_prepare`.

findings.evidence: receipt-main-only-integration/design.md says the derived-merge route is covered only through `RederivationFailed` -> integration repair -> `advance_after_repair`. `main_only_integration` excludes only `generated_files` from `dev-platform/checks.toml`, so derived or spec paths outside that set count as a difference (task_content_identity.py, `differing = ... - generated`).
findings.summary: Item 1 of the outcome also covers derived merges. T2's proof reaches only the `advance_after_repair` path, which runs after an integration repair or after a derived merge that raised RederivationFailed. A derived merge that succeeds and changes archive-derived specs is not in the `generated` set. If such a merge changes the identity, the receipt resets even though the change comes only from main.
